locator: I q.2 a.3 arg. 2: omnia quae apparent in mundo, possunt compleri per alia principia, supposito quod Deus non sit
interpretation: The naturalist parsimony objection in Aquinas' own text: natural things reduce to nature as their principle, purposive things to human reason or will, so positing God is unnecessary. Recorded as an objection to the arrow-and-archer premise; ad 2 answers it (nature works for a determinate end by a higher agent's direction).
